definition: A stepped temple platform of mud brick built in Mesopotamian cities, usually with a shrine at the top. Kings and priests maintained these towers as the centre of a city's cult.
A writing system that pressed wedge-shaped marks into damp clay with a cut reed. It was used for Sumerian, Akkadian, and other languages for more than three thousand years.
The Babylonian creation poem, named for its opening words, 'when on high.' It tells how Marduk defeated Tiamat and made the world, and it was recited at Babylon's New Year festival.
A group of Mesopotamian gods, often connected with the underworld and with deciding the fate of the dead. In the story of Inanna's descent they are the judges who condemn her.
In Sumerian myth, the me are fundamental powers or decrees that define civilised life, such as kingship, craft, and music. One poem tells how Inanna carried them away from Enki's shrine at Eridu.
A legendary king of Uruk and, in later tradition, the father of Gilgamesh. Two Sumerian poems tell of his adventures during a campaign against the city of Aratta.
One of the earliest and largest cities of southern Mesopotamia, closely associated with Gilgamesh and Inanna. Its ruins lie at Warka in modern Iraq.
The distant forest in the Gilgamesh epic where the guardian Humbaba lives. Its exact location is uncertain, but the poem places it in mountains to the west or north-west.
One of the oldest cities of southern Mesopotamia, home of the god Enki and his temple. The Sumerian King List names it as the first city to hold kingship when kingship came down from heaven.
Wise semi-divine sages in Mesopotamian tradition, often shown as fish-cloaked figures. They were credited with teaching crafts and rituals to the earliest human beings.
